role.altitude: The psychiatric aide keeps being with patients: watching areas, de-escalating, encouraging activities and joining in; checking restriction lists, logging leaves, ordering by phone and updating boards shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Using the ward tablet for quick, accurate logs
role.ambitious_version: An aide who spends the administration time saved on activities and talks with patients.

tasks.short: Check each patient's current restriction level, watch and accompany patients to maintain patients' restrictions to assigned areas, talk with patients who want to leave and log leaves and returns.

steps.what: Psychiatric aide checks each patient's current restriction level and leave rights at shift start
Psychiatric aide watches doors and movements and accompanies patients to keep them in assigned areas
Psychiatric aide talks with patients who want to leave their area and calms tension
Psychiatric aide logs patients' leaves and returns

tasks.design: The ward overview in the patient record shows each patient's current restriction level and leave rights as set by the psychiatrist or nurse, instead of a paper list rewritten each shift. Leaves and returns are logged on the ward tablet, which records the time; the aide still logs each one. Watching, accompanying and calming patients stay fully with the aide.
tasks.previous_blocker: Restriction lists were copied by hand at each handover.
tasks.enabler_now: Ward overviews in the patient record and tablets on the ward.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a patient is about to run.

reach.learn: Whether changes reach the floor faster.

evidence.claim: Large-scale processing of health data is on the list of processing that needs a DPIA.
Restrictions on freedom in mental health care rest on compulsory care laws and must be recorded.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping patients in assigned areas; restraint is outside.
Input contract for s1: restriction levels and leave rights entered by the psychiatrist or nurse in the record when they change, as today.
Watching and talking keep their full time. s1 keeps 60 because the overview replaces rewriting the paper list and reading it stays; s4 keeps 90 because only writing the time and name goes.
research_questions: Are handover mistakes about restrictions fewer?

incremental.description: Psychiatric aide corrects missed leave taps at shift end.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: restriction changes are often entered late, so the aide still checks with the nurse and s1 keeps 80 (3.8); high: the overview is current (6.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the activity schedule, prepare materials, encourage patient participation in social, educational or recreational activities and supervise them, and note participation.

steps.what: Psychiatric aide plans the weekly activity schedule with the activity therapist
Psychiatric aide prepares materials and the room
Psychiatric aide encourages patient participation and supervises the activities
Psychiatric aide notes who took part in the record

tasks.design: The activity schedule sits in a shared ward planner instead of a whiteboard and paper copies. Participation is ticked per patient on the ward tablet, which writes it to the record, with a free note only for something notable. Encouraging and supervising stay fully human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Participation was written as free text per patient after each activity.
tasks.enabler_now: Ward planners and tick lists on tablets.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a withdrawn patient to join in.

reach.learn: Whether participation data show which activities work.

evidence.claim: Ward tablets can record tick lists into the patient record.

assumptions: Boundary: organising and supervising activities; therapy sessions are outside.
Encouraging and supervising keep their full time.
s4 is part of recording behaviour and progress, which sibling task 31-1133.00:18697 covers; its saving is counted there, so s4 keeps its full time here.

incremental.description: Psychiatric aide updates the planner when activities change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few planned activities, so copying the schedule was little work and s1 keeps 95 (0.5); high: wards with daily group activities (2.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Complete administrative tasks: entering orders into the computer, answering telephone calls, maintaining facility information and keeping ward patient lists and boards current.

steps.what: Psychiatric aide enters orders into the computer for meals, supplies and transport: every order today, only special orders and transport after the change
Psychiatric aide checks the day's diet orders from the record: each patient's diet, allergies and meal against the record, and the kitchen it goes to
Psychiatric aide releases the checked diet orders to the kitchen system
Psychiatric aide checks the supply reorder from par levels: items and quantities against what the ward uses, and the store it goes to
Psychiatric aide releases the checked supply reorder to the store
Psychiatric aide answers telephone calls from families and departments
Psychiatric aide maintains facility information and writes repair requests: by phone today, on the facility service form after the change
Psychiatric aide checks the repair request: room, fault, urgency and the facility team it goes to
Psychiatric aide submits the checked repair request to the facility team
Psychiatric aide follows up repair status: by calling back today, by reading the form's status after the change
Psychiatric aide keeps ward patient lists and boards current

tasks.design: Diet orders go from the patient record to the kitchen system, and ward supplies reorder from par levels agreed with the store, so the aide checks each generated list and releases it once instead of entering every order. Repairs are written on the facility service form, checked and submitted once, and the form shows status instead of calling back. The ward board takes admissions, discharges and rooms from the record. Phone calls stay with the aide.

approvals.approved_version: The day's diet orders per patient exactly as checked by the aide in s1b, released once to the kitchen system for that day; any change needs a new check.
The supply reorder with items and quantities exactly as checked by the aide in s1d, released once to the store; any change needs a new check.
The repair request with room, fault and urgency exactly as checked by the aide in s3b, submitted once to the facility team's queue; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Orders, repairs and boards were handled by phone and retyping.
tasks.enabler_now: Links from the record to kitchen and stock systems, and facility service forms.
tasks.human_edge: Handling a distressed family member on the phone.

evidence.claim: Records apps with notifications replace paper and phone glue.
Large-scale processing of health data needs a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: ward administration; care is outside.
Input contract for s1: diets entered by nurses in the record and par levels set with the store; about 70% of orders follow from them; the rest are entered by hand; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: admissions, discharges and rooms from the record, entered by the admission office.

Phone calls keep their full time. s1 keeps 45 for special orders and transport; the two list checks and releases keep their full time. Writing, checking and submitting repair requests keep their full time; s3s keeps 20 for reading status.
unknowns: Share of orders that are non-standard.
research_questions: Do wrong meals or missing supplies fall?

already_counted.description: Psychiatric aide checks generated order lists.

incremental.description: Psychiatric aide reviews par levels with the store.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: wards with many special orders, so s1 keeps 70 (19.6); high: about 70% of orders follow from diets and par levels (26.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in recreational activities with patients, including card games, sports or television viewing, observe mood and contact, and note what stands out.

steps.what: Psychiatric aide participates in recreational activities with patients: card games, sports or television viewing
Psychiatric aide observes patients' mood and contact during the activity
Psychiatric aide notes what stands out in the record

tasks.design: Taking part and observing stay fully human. Notes use a short pick list for mood and contact on the ward tablet, with free text only for what needs words. The ward note belongs to the patient records task 31-1133.00:18697 and is priced there; taking part and observing do not change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked it; this is time with patients.
tasks.human_edge: Being good company to someone who is unwell.

reach.learn: Whether short structured notes help spot changes.

evidence.claim: Pick lists on tablets shorten routine notes.

assumptions: Boundary: recreation with patients and notes about it.
Taking part and observing keep their full time.
s3 is part of recording behaviour and progress, which sibling task 31-1133.00:18697 covers; its saving is counted there, so s3 keeps its full time here.
unknowns: How often notable observations are made.

incremental.description: No upkeep in this task; keeping the mood and contact pick list current is counted with sibling task 31-1133.00:18697.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No saving in this task: the only changed step belongs to sibling task 31-1133.00:18697.
